transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You're carrying the valley in your eyes. Don't let the dark drink it from you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: There is nothing left to drink but dust and old habits.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Keep your voice down, or the things in those stone houses will wake.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Let them wake. I only need to know where they took the boy.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I don't know names anymore, only shadows and the breathing behind walls.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: His name is Omar. I have walked until my feet are stone to find him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I cannot show you the way. I only know the edges of this square. Forty years, maybe fifty, counting by the cold in my bones.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You stayed still while the world rotted around you.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I stayed alive. That is the only trick I know. Survival is a heavy coat, even here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Heavy coat when there is nowhere to wear it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The ones in the high windows watch to see who breaks first. Jinn, old ones, ranking themselves by how close they dare sit to the oil.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Who sits at the head of it all.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There is a king — say it soft. Between fire and will, ancient and hungry. Everything here reports to him. Omar is kept, not lost. The king chose to hold him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: And the girl at the gate.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: She is his daughter. Whatever she showed you when you passed — it was not kindness. She reads what you carry and she remembers it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I see my failure every time I close my eyes. I do not need a mirror.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Look at the bubbling pool. The pale hands — those are the ones who bargained wrong. The pool took their thoughts and left the rest reaching.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It was my dare that sent Omar here. I dared him to insult the well. A hand rose and took him. That is my fault.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You say it flat, like a man who has already judged himself and moved past it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: There is nothing left to feel about it. I just need the words.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You are empty — that is worse than fear. The dark has nothing to grab in you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then let it try. Give me the fire.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There is a light they fear. When it is called, the hands sink and the watchers go quiet. But speaking of it makes the shadows lean in.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Let them lean. I am tired of whispering.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: It burns the one who holds it as much as the one it strikes. Ash does not fear the flame — but you are still breathing, and that matters.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Make me real again. Give me the words.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My jaw aches. My name — was it Hassan? No... the fog is thick today.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Your name is Hanash. Hold onto it for one more minute.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: A window just went dark. They are listening. The heavy fluid is churning. I am bleeding just reaching for this.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My eyes are on you. I am not moving.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Use it only when the pale hands touch you — not before. Call it early and it burns out before the dark does.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: When they touch. Not before.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: One last thing. If something speaks in Omar's voice and the shape of it is almost right — walk past it. The dark has had longer to practice than you have been alive.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I would know his voice in any dark.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break. Say it once.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't repeat it. The square listens for echoes. There is one more — harder to give. My hands won't stop.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am still here.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Prayer for the lost: Light find my hand. Light find my path. Let the Sword of Light answer, and let it fade when the shadows loosen. Never say it twice in the same dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I have both. I'll hold them until the hands reach.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Use the first when you feel yourself going hollow. Use the second when they touch you. The order matters.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: First to hold, second to push. I have it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I gave you what forty years of hiding couldn't. That costs more than memory.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't waste it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Take my name back to the sun. Tell them Hanash held the line.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will say it where the light can hear it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: That is a better end than mine — to be a story in a living mouth.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Stay standing, old man.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Go. Find a better end than mine.
